synopsis: The research had no internal sensor specifications or recordings, and sensor selection remained unconfirmed across chapters; the October 2026 plan therefore recommends a sensor-agnostic architecture, with sensor simulation selected only after a shortlist is known [f7, f8, f287, f8257, f485, f507, f8796]. A programme starting in October 2026 could realistically have software-in-the-loop simulation with partly validated sensor models working by mid-2027, but each sensor type needs its own credibility argument and simulation can replace only part—not most—of physical sensor testing [f65, f1577, f4407]. Sensor/environment fidelity is identified as a leading uncertainty precisely where risk lies: no accepted off-road qualification method was found for dust, snow or fog, glare-related effects are poorly validated, and physical characterization is recommended at mounting-geometry extremes and in degraded visibility [f10424, f212, f331, f4406, f7885]. Existing recordings cannot establish performance for unrecorded sensor types or positions, and rare-event methods cannot substantiate failure modes whose sensor physics the simulation omits [f3729, f5240, f6853]. Detection is necessary for braking but insufficient for safe overall performance: normal production tasks can appear dangerous to sensors, and improving sensors alone does not resolve task-dependent nuisance braking [f11302, f124, f3487, f11766].
